title: Load balancer: round-robin with health checks
summary: Distribute incoming requests across healthy backend servers sequentially. Filters out unhealthy instances before calculating the round-robin index. O(1) routing.
code: # Distribute requests across healthy servers in round-robin sequence.
if is_healthy and server in self.servers:
active = [s for s in self.servers if s in self.healthy]
triggers: evenly distribute requests among a dynamic pool of backend instances
handle backend server failures and health updates without dropping traffic
prompts: A gateway receives HTTP requests and forwards them to a cluster of worker nodes in turn, skipping any nodes currently reporting downtime.
Design a service proxy that registers API replicas and balances client queries evenly across all healthy backends.
invariant: Traffic is only routed to servers present in both self.servers and self.healthy; the cursor advances modulo the active server count.
mantra: Filter by health, modulo over active, advance the cursor.
pitfalls: Advancing cursor using total servers instead of healthy servers causes uneven distribution or out-of-range indexing.
Failing to handle an empty healthy pool leads to division by zero on modulo.
Removing or marking unhealthy must not leave phantom entries in the healthy set.

anchors.name: Design a Load Balancer
anchors.trick: Keep registered server order stable; filter to active pool before modulo selection.
